span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An asymmetric interplay of excitation and inhibition within the beta cycle produces an uninformative upswing and an informative downswing of spiking
span.note: duplicate of: mechanisms[3]

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Beta rhythms are tuned to large-scale network communication rather than local processing, which is why choice information becomes separated in time from local excitability
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Downstream ensembles read out the two rhythms with different integration windows, beta's extending past the moment of peak synchronous input to catch the later information peak
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: beta spiking is proposed to come from an asymmetric interplay of excitation and inhibition, giving an uninformative upswing and an informative downswing at similar spike counts
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the two bands are read as two network scales, gamma as local bottom-up processing and beta as top-down linkage to a larger cortical network
span.note: status: the paper's own words: may reflect
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: downstream ensembles may integrate over different windows in the two bands, with the beta window reaching past peak synchrony to the later information peak
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: theta may regulate the faster scales, since theta phase predicts beta and gamma amplitude
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: parietal spiking may multiplex decision signals into a beta and a gamma channel
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Mutual information estimates could have been inflated at phase bins containing few spikes; the authors re-ran the analysis with stratified spike counts.
span.note: what this limits: every mutual-information value: MI ESTIMATION MAY HAVE BEEN BIASED BY THE DIFFERING SPIKE COUNTS AT DIFFERENT PHASES OF ACTIVITY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: How the beta-band dissociation between spiking and information is generated, and how downstream populations could read it out, is left open.
span.note: what this limits: the mechanism behind the beta dissociation: it RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW THE ACTIVITY CAN BE GENERATED AND HOW OTHER NEURONAL POPULATIONS CAN DECODE SUCH ACTIVITY EFFICIENTLY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how such a code is generated and how any downstream population could read it efficiently is left open
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[1] · what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - generation and readout both open
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the proposed source of the beta dissociation - the beta to gamma phase difference - was tested and did not correlate with it
span.note: what this limits: the paper's own candidate explanation, which it tested and rejected: WE OBSERVED NO CORRELATION BETWEEN THE BETA-GAMMA PHASE DIFFERENCE AND THE MOMENT OF THE BETA CHOICE-MI
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the primary modulation statistic assumes a single concentration across phase bins and cannot see multimodal modulation, so a second statistic had to be run
span.note: what this limits: the modulation-strength statistic: THE MEAN RESULTANT LENGTH R ASSUMES A UNIMODAL CONCENTRATION ... IT IS INSENSITIVE TO MORE COMPLEX FORMS OF MODULATION SUCH AS MULTIMODAL MODULATIONS - so the analysis was REPEATED using entropy-based permutation statistics
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: MI is positively biased for smaller samples and spuriously high for phase bins with few spikes, and spike counts differ across phases, so MI had to be reestimated with the counts equal across phase bins
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the correction reported: WE REESTIMATED MI WHILE STRATIFYING SPIKE COUNTS TO BE EQUAL ACROSS PHASE BINS ... THE PATTERN ... PERSISTED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the unit of analysis is mixed: 149 units of which only 45 are single units, the rest multiunit
span.note: what this limits: what a 'unit' means in every count here: 149 UNITS [97 ... (31 SINGLE UNITS AND 66 MULTIUNITS) FOR MONKEY C AND 52 (14 SINGLE UNITS AND 38 MULTIUNITS) FOR MONKEY R]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: what this limits: the spatial reach of the gamma result: THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THE ELECTRODE TIPS OF THE RECORDING PAIRS INFLUENCED THE SFC, comparing pairs at a median separation of 1.07 mm against the farther half

span.label: the whole analysis repeated while STRATIFYING the number of spikes at each phase bin
span.note: eliminates: spike count as the driver of mutual information - MI rises with the amount of data, so a phase bin with more spikes would show more MI whether or not the phase carries anything

span.label: THE ESTIMATOR'S OWN BIAS WOULD HAVE PRODUCED THE RESULT: mutual information runs high on small samples, the number of spikes differs from phase bin to phase bin, so phase-dependent information is exactly what a biased estimator would manufacture here

span.label: and it is answered twice over - each bin's estimate is restricted to the smallest bin's sample size, and spikes in excess of that minimum are deleted at random and the estimate repeated a thousand times
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: INFORMATION AND RATE ARE NOT THE SAME QUANTITY: in the beta band the spike count is symmetric about its preferred phase while the information is not, and the two peak at different times
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: so a rate-based reading of this code would place the information at the wrong moment - and in the gamma band, where the two do coincide, it would be right
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE NULL IS THE FINDING: removing the spike count's prediction leaves the beta information still modulated but flattens the gamma information entirely, so the same control analysis reports independence in one band and dependence in the other

span.label: THE HEADLINE STATISTIC NAMES ITS OWN BLIND SPOT: the resultant length assumes one concentration across phase bins and is insensitive to multimodal modulation, which is why an entropy measure is run beside it

span.label: A UNIT HERE IS TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF OBJECT: 45 single units and 104 multiunits, and every count in the paper is reported split rather than pooled

span.label: qualifies → its own explanation of the beta dissociation, by testing the beta to gamma phase difference against it and finding no relationship
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS THE REFERENCE RHYTHM. 'Beta-gamma phase-phase coupling COULD CONTRIBUTE TO THE TEMPORAL LOCALIZATION OF THE CHOICE-MI with respect to the beta [rhythm].' The paper qualifies its own account by naming what the localisation is measured AGAINST - a self-qualification, which is the rarer and more careful use of this type. Q-444. CORRECTED AT Q-489: the quote originally ended at 'could contribute to the temporal localization of the choice-MI' - THE HYPOTHESIS HALF OF THE SPAN. The paper then rejects it: 'HOWEVER, WE OBSERVED NO CORRELATION between the beta-gamma phase difference and the moment of the beta choice-MI phase histogram on a single-spike LFP level.' The target already said 'finding no relationship', so the row's prose was right and its EVIDENCE recorded the possibility rather than the finding. Widened through the reversal.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

HOWEVER, WE OBSERVED NO CORRELATION BETWEEN THE BETA-GAMMA PHASE DIFFERENCE AND THE MOMENT OF THE BETA CHOICE-MI PHASE HISTOGRAM ON A SINGLE-SPIKE LFP LEVEL.' span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER INFORMATION SITS AT ONE PHASE OR SPREADS ACROSS THE CYCLE. 'During visual stimulation in primate primary visual cortex, THE GAMMA ACTIVITY ENHANCES SELECTIVITY, PRIMARILY AT AROUND PEAK EXCITABILITY. However, during working memory demands in primate prefrontal cortex, information about sequentially presented objects occurs AT DIFFERENT TIMES WITH RESPECT TO THE BETA ACTIVITY.' Both are phase-referenced codes; they differ on whether one phase carries the information or several do, which is what makes the second a sequence rather than a gain.
